questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why people in rich countries are happier
The idea of flourishing and what a big study found about it
How to grow flowers and plants at home
Why people feel less happy after the age of 50
questions.why: They discuss the idea of 'flourishing' and the findings of the Global Flourishing Study.

options: It is another word for being rich
It means feeling physically healthy, even if you are not always happy
It is about your whole life being good, not just wellbeing
It is an old idea that nobody uses now
questions.why: She says it's not just about wellbeing – 'it's about your whole life being good'.

questions.q: Do Phil and Georgie feel they are flourishing?
options: Yes, they both feel happy with their lives
Georgie does, but Phil doesn't
Phil does, but Georgie isn't sure about her own life
Neither of them feels they are
questions.why: Georgie says everything's going well, and Phil says he thinks the same.

questions.q: How big was the Global Flourishing Study?
options: About 2,000 people in 12 countries
About 20,000 people in 200 countries
About 22,000 people in 20 countries
Over 200,000 people in 22 countries
questions.why: Phil says it's a survey of over 200,000 people in 22 countries.

questions.q: According to psychologist Dr Peter Olusoga, what did middle-income countries like Mexico score highly on?
options: Money, income and financial security for families
Relationships, kindness and social connection
Health and physical fitness
Education and careers
questions.why: He says middle-income countries scored highly on relationships, kindness and social cohesion.

questions.q: What did the study find about age?
options: Young people flourished the most
Age made no difference at all
Flourishing dropped for most people after they retired
Flourishing increased after the age of 50
questions.why: Georgie says that across all countries, flourishing increased after the age of 50.

questions.q: Which of these does Peter Olusoga NOT suggest to help us flourish?
options: Working longer hours to earn more
Being thankful for the things that we already have
Showing kindness to others
Enjoying our small successes
questions.why: He suggests gratitude, kindness and celebrating small wins, but not working more.

questions.q: Why does Phil mention the saying about a journey of a thousand miles?
options: To suggest that travel makes people flourish
To say that flourishing takes a very long time to measure properly
To show that small steps and successes really matter
To explain why some countries scored badly
questions.why: He uses it to say savouring each small win along the way is vital to flourishing.
